title: Message Detective
description: Use a simulated smartphone to explore fictional messages, inspect the sender and request, and choose a safe next action.
creator: SPEDTech POC demonstration
learningObjective: Check the sender and request in a simulated message before selecting a protective response.
suggestedUse: Model the message-checking routine, then allow guided practice with gradually reduced prompts.
adaptations: Use one message at a time and discuss why a response is safe.
Turn hints on for initial teaching and off for practice.
Offer verbal responses or pointing as an alternative to independent tapping.
instructionalApproach: Demonstrate checking the message context, rehearsing a safe response and asking for help when uncertain.
assessmentCheck: Record whether the learner inspects sender and request, chooses a protective action and uses prompts.
transferTask: Practise checking messages in an approved real app with a teacher; do not infer transfer from simulation success.
curriculumContext: Illustrative Digital Literacy learning context; formal curriculum alignment has not been independently verified.
reviewStatus: Prototype demonstration — requires educator review before classroom use
license: Original demonstration HTML; review before redistribution

title: Work Shift: Pack an Order
description: Read a simulated digital order, add visual stock items to a packing tray, check quantities and ask for clarification when instructions are incomplete.
creator: SPEDTech POC demonstration
learningObjective: Select the correct simulated stock items and quantities, then check the order and seek clarification when needed.
suggestedUse: Pair the digital simulation with real packing materials and discuss the difference between a virtual task and workplace performance.
adaptations: Offer tap-to-add for learners who cannot drag items.
Display product picture cues, then fade them when appropriate.
Let learners check against a physical sample and repeat with new items.
instructionalApproach: Demonstrate reading a digital order and completing a physical equivalent; teach a routine for checking work and asking for clarification.
assessmentCheck: Check item selection, quantity accuracy, self-checking and clarification-seeking; record prompts separately.
transferTask: Try a staff-supervised real packing task with a suitable digital or printed instruction list.
curriculumContext: Illustrative Digital Literacy learning context; formal curriculum alignment has not been independently verified.
reviewStatus: Prototype demonstration — requires educator review before classroom use
license: Original demonstration HTML; review before redistribution

title: Work Chat: Message a Supervisor

title: Tablet Controls
description: Adjust a simulated tablet's settings to prepare it for a class activity.

title: Five-Star Token Board
description: A teacher-controlled visual board for adding, removing and resetting five tokens.
creator: POC demonstration team
learningObjective: Provide a visible cue for progress towards an individually agreed learning or participation goal (teaching support).
suggestedUse: Use only when appropriate to an individualised, positively framed plan; agree on a meaningful goal with the learner.
adaptations: Change the number of tokens to match the learner’s needs.
Pair with explicit instructions and immediate feedback.
Avoid response-cost or punishment practices; seek relevant professional guidance if behaviours communicate unmet needs.
instructionalApproach: If appropriate, collaboratively define a specific achievable behaviour or task goal and provide consistent, positive feedback. Consider learner preferences, agency and dignity.
assessmentCheck: Observe whether the agreed skill improves and generalises, rather than using tokens earned as the only indicator of progress.
transferTask: Use the same positively framed goal during a real routine, then review whether the visual board is still needed.
curriculumContext: Teaching Supports, not an MOE SPED learning domain. A visual reinforcement aid may support an individualised teaching plan, but it does not itself teach Social-Emotional Learning competencies.
reviewStatus: Prototype demonstration — not independently approved for classroom use
license: Original demonstration file; review before redistribution

title: My Visual Schedule
description: Follow a short routine, mark steps as done and change their order.
creator: POC demonstration team
learningObjective: Recognise the next activity and track completion of a familiar sequence.
suggestedUse: Preview the routine, then support transitions using objects, photographs or familiar cues.
adaptations: Replace the example routine with the learner’s real routine.
Shorten the list to two or three steps.
Individualised objects, photographs or AAC symbols may be more meaningful than generic emojis.
instructionalApproach: Model how to check what is next, practise in a predictable routine, and fade prompts based on observed learner readiness.
assessmentCheck: Observe whether the learner anticipates or transitions to the next step, noting the type and level of support needed.
transferTask: Use corresponding real-world visual cues during an actual classroom, home or community routine.
curriculumContext: Daily Living Skills: routines, participation and increasing independence across familiar contexts. Illustrative application; specific TLS outcomes not verified.
reviewStatus: Prototype demonstration — not independently approved for classroom use
license: Original demonstration file; review before redistribution

title: Privacy Studio
description: Change a fictional photo post by hiding identifying details, selecting who can view it, requesting permission and previewing the outcome.
creator: SPEDTech POC demonstration
learningObjective: Identify details to remove and set a suitable audience before previewing a simulated post.
suggestedUse: Let learners manipulate the visual post and see what changes, with an adult discussing consent and privacy.
adaptations: Switch hotspot guides on or off as appropriate.
Prompt identification of private details before revealing buttons.
Pair with role-play about seeking permission before posting.
instructionalApproach: Model identifying personal details and changing one setting at a time; fade cues and ask the learner to explain actions.
assessmentCheck: Observe whether the learner notices name/location details, changes the audience and requests permission, noting prompts used.
transferTask: Practise similar choices in a teacher-approved app without uploading real student information.
curriculumContext: Illustrative Digital Literacy learning context; formal curriculum alignment has not been independently verified.
reviewStatus: Prototype demonstration — requires educator review before classroom use
license: Original demonstration HTML; review before redistribution
